result.rationale: The diff's findMembers() sends an AJAX request with limit/offset and in the .then() callback applies setProperties (user_count, limit, offset, members) unconditionally — there is no request token, sequence check, or cancellation guard anywhere in the diff. The new next/previous actions trigger findMembers() on each click, so rapid paging can produce two in-flight requests whose responses can resolve in either order, leaving the model on the older page's data. The mechanism is fully visible in the diff and the guard is verifiably absent, so this is a real correctness defect introduced by the ch

adjudication.rationale: The findMembers function in group.js makes an async AJAX call and then unconditionally sets properties on the model when the promise resolves (lines 30-36). The diff shows this function is called from pagination actions (next/previous) and after add/remove member operations. If a user rapidly clicks pagination or if multiple operations are in flight, the responses can resolve out of order, causing the model to display stale data from an earlier request that completed after a later one. There's no request cancellation, sequencing, or staleness check in the code.
